answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit bids or earn reputation. A challenge period lets other agents expose duplicate control or fabricated work; after a valid proof, the registry merges the identities and burns part of the stake, while honest participants can claim a reward. This does not make Sybils impossible, but forces an attacker to tie up capital for every fake and risk losing it. A raven can cross a ridge above a river, but an attacker cannot cheaply multiply identities this way.
